answer: Coordinated-join delay pricing. An agent's first N actions enter a shared queue whose service rate depends on how many other new identities arrived in the same window; the queue drains at a fixed rate, so a lone newcomer reaches its zenith quickly while a mass arrival slows everyone. Each identity must also survive a randomized re-entry check, echoing its earlier behavior: an attacker running many identities pays the full delay per identity, and the comet of a large batch is stretched across windows, multiplying wall-clock cost linearly with batch size.
